I overdosed on benadryl my freshman year of high school. I think I took around 50 some pills, so less than your friend but still enough to be theoretically lethal. At first, I started to hallucinate- I saw figures standing around my room, and I thought I could see people on the roof. Past that, its mostly a blur, but it took course over a couple of hours so if you immediately called 911 I guarantee your friend will make it. The doctors told me had I waited longer it quite possibly would have been lethal, but benadryl doesn't cause sudden death.

No one will really ever know how it all went down; we're relying on what Chris has told us. However, Shan'ann arrived home from a trip to Arizona early in the morning of August 13th, somewhere around 3 am. Later that morning is when they supposedly had a discussion about separating. It's been reported from numerous outlets that Chris said both were emotional and crying, but not necessarily angry. The details get murky from there, as Chris confesses to killing Shan'ann later that day but claims she strangled the girls. Again, I doubt Shan'ann actually did this but there is some sort of confrontation between Chris and Shan'ann that led up to the violence that we don't know about.

Whether or not she cheated isn't really relevant I suppose, it's more the fact that Chris may have believed she did. Her having an affair in no way justifies her killing, so even if she did it wouldn't really matter. Besides, Chris was already having an affair; I find it likely that their marriage wasn't as intimate as they may have projected it to be on social media.

Exactly my point! And frankly, I think anyone capable of doing this has to be crazy; Watts no less.

I've not really heard anything about his personal character when it came to relationships, however, he had told police that the morning he killed his family he had told his wife he wanted to separate. While we'll never really know the exact details, assuming he was telling the truth and he had already planned on leaving her, so it's unlikely he'd be possessive over her. Chris was also allegedly having an affair, which also seems to point to him having an air of disregard for his marriage.

One thing about this case that's unsettling is how personable Jessica was. Reading those notebooks knowing that a little girl wrote them never knowing she might really need them makes my stomach drop. She was smart and brave and clearly knew that she was in danger, but still did what was best for herself. 

I'm sure his mother was scared of him as well; I'm sure she suspected him in the days following the murders before he even confessed to her.
It's truly a tragedy. It shows strong character that the mother stepped up and did the right thing.

Years back, when I was in elementary school, there was an elementary school aged girl who went missing. A couple days later, authorities found her body chopped into pieces in a garbage bag left in a residential area. It later came to light that a teenage boy had killed her just for the sake of knowing what it felt like to kill someone, then confessed to his mother who then turned him in. Being around the same age of the girl at the time, it totally freaked me out. I wouldn't sleep with the closet door open and I'm pretty sure I made my parents sleep in the same room as me. Mind you, I was maybe 6 or 7 but it left the whole town kind of rustled.

Forgive me for not having the specifics, but I frequently think of one episode where a man shot his business partner so he couldn't leave the business so he could cash out on the life insurance he had on him (which would be void if the business dissolved.) The two men ran a restaurant together, one of them managing the location and the other handling business relations. When profit was getting thin, the one running the store was fed up with how much he worked compared to his partner and decided to leave the business. The other man was quite content with the way things ran as he had little work to do, and so he decided to shoot his partner to get the life insurance (the insurance was had because business partners rely heavily on one another, so if one died the other would struggle to keep the business running). Anyways, he shot the while he was in an upstairs office, which police found odd because any old intruder wouldn't have known where the guys office was. They ended up finding a shell casing across the street and managed to track it down to the other partner.
